# SlowGo

> Navigation for golf carts and low-speed vehicles. SlowGo builds routes that stay
> on roads posted 35 mph and under wherever possible — the LSV line in Florida —
> and says so plainly when a trip can't avoid something faster. Where a golf cart
> may ride is its county's or city's call; SlowGo does not decide that. A product
> of BackRoad Apps LLC.

SlowGo v1.0 is released. The iOS app is on the App Store as of 25 August 2026, free
to start, at https://slowgoapp.com/go. Android comes later.

## Status and coverage

- Routing is live in **Florida and Georgia** only. Those two states are where
  SlowGo's speed-limit data is checked today.
- Outside Florida and Georgia you can search, browse the map, and plan a ride,
  but SlowGo will not start a turn-by-turn route. States are added one at a time,
  after their roads are checked, rather than guessed at.
- Works with CarPlay. Plug the phone in and the route, the turn-by-turn card and
  the same speed labels show on the cart's screen; saved favorites can be chosen
  and a ride started from the screen; the phone can stay locked in the cupholder.
- Built with cart communities in mind — The Villages, Hilton Head, Peachtree City,
  Fire Island, and similar places.

## How routing works

- **Green** — roads posted 35 mph and under, the LSV line. This is the default,
  and most rides never leave it. It is not a statement that a golf cart may use
  the road: that is the county's or city's designation.
- **Amber** — roads posted 36 to 45 mph. Offered only if the rider opts in to
  faster stretches, and the length of the stretch is shown before the ride starts.
- **NoGo** — no route exists that stays on 35-and-under roads. SlowGo says so
  rather than quietly routing onto a fast road.
- Roads confirmed above 45 mph are never routed along.
- Where a road carries no posted limit in the map data, SlowGo judges it by road
  type, labels it as judged, and never invents a number.
- Every route is speed-checked before the Start button unlocks. A check that
  can't finish leaves the button locked.
- Where a route uses a material stretch of path, SlowGo also checks whether that
  path has cart-access notes recorded on the shared map. That check holds Start
  only while it is pending; the answer is disclosed, never used to block, and an
  absent note is treated as missing information rather than a prohibition. SlowGo
  does not determine whether a route is legal for a given cart.

## Privacy posture

- No accounts, no sign-in, no ads, no ad tracking.
- Route requests are processed on a first-party server and are not kept beyond
  short-lived technical logs.
- Favorites and trip history stay on the device. Trip start and end points are
  stored roughly, not precisely.

- [Terms of Service](https://slowgoapp.com/terms): the terms of use, including the
  safety rules for riding.
